def modular_derangements(n, k):
    """Count permutations avoiding differences divisible by k.

    A permutation p of {1, 2, ..., n} is a bijection from {1, ..., n} to
    itself; write p(i) for the value at position i. Count the permutations
    p such that for EVERY position i (1 <= i <= n), the difference
    p(i) - i is NOT divisible by k. (Zero counts as divisible by k, so in
    particular p(i) = i is always forbidden.)

    Input domain: n and k are integers with 1 <= n <= 200 and
    1 <= k <= 300. Within these bounds a correct solution must run in
    well under 0.1 seconds per input in CPython.

    Output: the exact number of such permutations, as a Python int
    (it may be astronomically large -- hundreds of digits; no rounding,
    no modulus).

    Edge cases implied by the definition:
      - k == 1 divides every difference, so the answer is 0 for all n.
      - If k >= n then |p(i) - i| <= n - 1 < k, so the only forbidden
        assignments are fixed points p(i) = i, and the answer equals the
        number of derangements of n elements.

    Examples:
    >>> modular_derangements(4, 4)
    9
    >>> modular_derangements(4, 2)
    4
    >>> modular_derangements(3, 1)
    0
    """
